known_gaps_and_source_controls.control: FnDef resolution Err distinct from FnPtr
known_gaps_and_source_controls.fact: fn-pointer, entry, and pending-ops controls exercise FnPtr resolution failure, not Err resolving a statically known FnDef. A valid monomorphic Rust FnDef normally supplies a resolvable definition; no source fixture is asserted for an artificial FnDef resolver Err. If code-level resolution Err needs coverage, add a compiler-level resolver/visitor unit control.

shim-plain/shim-seeded are copied Fn::call source controls whose standalone golden reports bodyless Shim. The neutralized source comments no longer claim bodyful/bodyless classification. Pinned Part 1 CI must inspect actual resolved InstanceKind/body; if bodyful, assert inner unresolved FnPtr is locally rejected.

Separate plain/seeded FnOnce(MaybeUninit<u16>) -> () sources are lowering probes only; wrapper and shim source return unit. Rust FnOnce call arguments are tuple-wrapped, and visitor transfers_shadow recognizes direct MaybeUninit/union Ty, so CI must prove a direct shadow arg reaches the guard. If not, these source probes do not establish guard coverage and a compiler-level visitor fixture with synthetic direct shadow arg is required.
Separate plain/seeded FnOnce() -> MaybeUninit<u16> controls provide no shadow argument and a shadow return; CI must establish bodyful Shim lowering and guard reachability.

seed_policy: Seeded variants use standalone supported std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping over ordinary initialized bytes; no raw_eq seed dependency.

coordinator_ci.plan: Run each plain and seeded harness separately. Inspect machine-readable instrumentation/safety properties by harness + source path + terminator site (not invented numeric IDs). For entry controls establish exactly one target, LoadArgument presence, u32 Check status and exactly one local FnPtr diagnostic; for pending-ops establish Check-before-Unsupported. Do not infer multiple checks from one substring golden. Expected Complete footer counts are runner formatting only, not evidence or assumed integrated outcomes.
